content:
The image shows a soybean field where most plants have matured and turned brown/tan (normal senescence), but a distinct row/strip of plants in the foreground and continuing into the field remains green — stems, leaves, and pods are still green while surrounding plants have fully senesced.

Key observations:
- Green stems and leaves persisting on specific plants while neighboring plants are fully brown and mature
- The green plants appear to retain their leaves and stems at harvest maturity
- This is a field-level view showing the contrast between green and senesced plants
- No obvious lesions, mold, or other fungal/bacterial symptoms visible
- The pattern is linear (row-based), consistent with a heritable or infection-based trait

This matches **Green_stem_disorder** precisely: "All or part of the soybean plant remains green while the rest of the plant or neighboring plants mature and senesce. Most commonly seen in stems, leaves, or pods remaining green with excessive retained leaves. Stems stay moist and green while pods may mature normally."
